newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products lifted higher by crude's takeoff.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products lifted higher by crude's takeoff.

text.p: Med oil products moved sharply higher after Feb Brent crude futures jumped more than $1 a barrel by the end of the day.
In gas oil, prices firmed $8 as futures were lifted by technical strength in NYMEX crude and heating oil.
"The market is stronger for sellers. There are more buyers out there this week," a broker said.
Premiums for 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil were seen at around cif high +$1 basis Genoa, up about $1 from levels done on Friday at around cif high -10 cents.

A small Russian was done into Yugoslavia at cif high +$1 basis Bar and a major offered an Italian at fob high Med quotes +$2.50 loading January 5-10. A cargo of low sulphur diesel was sought basis Sete to arrive January 1-5 but this was likely to be covered by an Algerian loading at Sete December 28-30.
Fuel oil prices drifted higher in the slipstream of stronger crude, but little activity was seen.
The French utility Electricite de France (EdF) has tendered to buy 36,00 tonnes of low sulphur cracked material for January delivery, but this has given minimal support to a market that looks long.

Traders said with delivery into three ports the tender was too fragmented to give encouragement to sellers. Cargoes were heard variously between $127.50 fob NWE for early Jan on 25kt and around $130 fob NWE for end Dec on 50kt.
Gasoline edged higher with the rally in crude oil that boosted Brent futures more than $1 a barrel for the most active February contract.
Premium unleaded cargoes were notionally valued at $220/$222 cif and fob at $211/$215.
Naphtha edged higher with crude but traders said supplies in both the Med and NWE were balanced to long with demand.
